questions.q: How did the East India Company transform from a trading body into a territorial power in Bengal?
answer: The East India Company came to India in 1600 to trade, but in Bengal it gradually seized political power.

answer.text: Conflict with Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah led to the Battle of Plassey in 1757, where Robert Clive defeated him, helped by the betrayal of his commander Mir Jafar. This was the Company's first great political victory.
In 1764 the Company defeated the combined armies of the Nawab of Awadh, the Mughal emperor and Mir Qasim at Buxar, confirming its dominance.
In 1765 the Mughal emperor granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa — the right to collect revenue — turning the trader into the real ruler of the richest province.

questions.q: Explain how the Subsidiary Alliance and the Doctrine of Lapse helped the Company expand.

answer.text: Introduced by Lord Wellesley, this system required an Indian ruler to keep a British army within his state and pay for it, not to employ other Europeans, and to accept a British Resident at his court. A ruler who could not pay had to give up territory. States such as Awadh and Hyderabad were tied down this way.

Introduced by Lord Dalhousie, this held that if a ruler died without a natural heir, his kingdom would 'lapse' to the Company. Adopted heirs were not recognised, and states such as Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur were annexed.
Together these policies let the Company absorb one state after another without always fighting wars.
